literal: Embrace in-between cool breeze to-pass-through, sallowness attained simple-woman's great rain-like eyes.
translation: Just because a cool breeze passed through the space between us during our embrace, the large, rain-like eyes of this simple girl have turned sallow.
modern: எங்கள் தழுவலுக்கு இடையே குளிர்ந்த காற்று புகுந்து சென்றதற்கே, இந்தப் பேதை பெண்ணின் பெரிய மழை போன்ற கண்கள் பசலை நிறத்தை அடைந்துவிட்டன.
explanation: This couplet describes the extreme sensitivity of the heroine's love and her inability to bear even the briefest separation. The hero remarks that during their tight embrace, a tiny gap occurred, allowing a cool breeze to pass between their bodies. This momentary and minute distance was felt so intensely by the naive heroine that her large, moist, rain-like eyes immediately lost their natural luster and turned sallow. The word 'pasappu' refers to the yellowing or paleness of the skin and eyes caused by the grief of separation, highlighting the depth of her attachment.
